summary:
The Veneto vine bulletin archive is REAL and I reached it, but NOT through the site search — the site search cannot see it at all.

SEARCH ENDPOINT (proven, not guessed): I fetched the homepage HTML and read the two <form> tags. The public endpoint is GET https://www.regione.veneto.it/web/guest/ricerca?globalSearchText={q}. I proved it actually filters with a control pair: "zqxwvzzz9911nonsense" -> "Nessun risultato" (0 items, 34669 bytes); "peronospora" -> "Mostrati 1 - 7 su 7 risultati" (7 items, 45439 bytes). A second, equivalent POST portlet action exists (_searchcontents_WAR_rvecontentsmanager_action=searchContentsAction) and returns identical counts.

THE SEARCH IS USELESS FOR THIS MISSION, and I measured why:
(1) It does NOT index /web/fitosanitario/. The page /web/fitosanitario/bollettini-viticoli contains the literal string "Oidio" 44 times and "Peronospora" 40 times. Searching "oidio" returns 3 results and that page is not among them; searching "peronospora" returns 7 and that page is not among them. So the bulletins are invisible to the site search.
(2) Multi-word queries are a loose OR sorted by date, not relevance: "bollettino vite" -> 2744, "difesa integrata vite" -> 3314, "bollettino fitosanitario" -> 2488, all returning the same generic newest-news list (Mostra del Cinema, meteo alerts).
(3) A language trap: Italian "vite" means both "grapevine" and "lives". Top hits for "vite peronospora" (366) were "Salvare Vite" (Saving Lives), a firefighters' book.
(4) Latin binomials do not work: "Erysiphe necator" -> "Nessun risultato" (0). "Plasmopara viticola" -> 40 hits that all matched only the token "viticola" (viticoltura/riconversione viticola), none about the pathogen. The bulletins themselves contain "Erysiphe" 0 times and "Plasmopara" 0 times — Veneto writes Italian common names (Oidio, Peronospora, Botrite, Tignoletta, Flavescenza dorata).

HOW I ACTUALLY FOUND THE ARCHIVE: by navigation. Searching "fitosanitario" surfaced articleGroupId=11979050 and an article "FITOS_home" (articleId=11987717). Fetching that article exposed the real UO Fitosanitario site menu, which contains the index.

THE INDEX (real, fetched): https://www.regione.veneto.it/web/fitosanitario/bollettini-fitosanitari (HTTP 200, 47736 bytes) links exactly three year pages: 2024, 2025, 2026. All were fetched HTTP 200.

WEEKLY VINE SERIES IS PROVEN. 2025: 20 vine issues, numbered N.1..N.20 with no gaps, 09/04/2025 -> 27/08/2025, day gaps [7,7,7,7,7,7,8,6,7,7,8,6,7,7,7,7,7,14,7], median 7. 2026: 20 vine issues, N.1..N.20 with no gaps, 09/04/2026 -> 27/08/2026, median 7. 2024: 18 inline full-text bulletins, 04/04/2024 -> 30/08/2024, median 7. The season runs April to late August, roughly 20 issues per year.

THREE DIFFERENT DELIVERY FORMATS ACROSS THREE YEARS — this matters for any collector: 2026 bulletins are native PDFs on regione.veneto.it under /documents/11979050/14345303/; 2025 bulletins are PDFs behind a Nextcloud public share on a DIFFERENT host, sharing.regione.veneto.it/index.php/s/{token} (append /download for the file); 2024 has NO PDFs at all — I searched that page for document links and found 0 — the 2024 bulletins exist only as inline HTML full text on /web/fitosanitario/bollettini-viticoli.

I downloaded 4 PDFs + saved the 2024 HTML page (5 samples, within the 6 cap) and confirmed content is real. All 4 PDFs have %PDF magic and %%EOF. pdftotext extracts 6373-8561 chars each. vite_2026_01.pdf reads "U.O. Fitosanitario / Bollettino n. 1 del 09 aprile 2026 / VITE" with ARPAV weather, a BBCH phenology table by grape variety (Pinot, Chardonnay, Glera, Garganega, Corvina, Merlot), pathogen status naming oidio/escoriosi/peronospora, RIMpro and Horta model risk simulations, Lobesia botrana trap catches, and named vineyard sites (S.Ambrogio VR, Collalbrigo TV, Istrana).

PDF GOTCHA I MEASURED: all four PDFs carry /Encrypt with /Filter/Standard. Naive zlib stream extraction returns 0 characters; I initially misread this as scanned images. pdftotext (poppler, present at /mingw64/bin) opens them fine. Any collector using a raw parser will silently get empty text.

PRE-2024: I could not find any. Probing the year-page pattern gave clean 404s for 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023 — and also 404 for 2027, which validates the probe rather than proving absence. The Liferay folder listing /documents/11979050/14345303/ is 404 (not browsable). A web-search snippet claimed the bollettini-viticoli page holds April 2023 dates; I fetched that page and it contains 21 date tokens, ALL 2024, and 0 for 2023 — the snippet is a stale index, and the live per-crop page appears to be overwritten in place each year. A suggested mirror host elezioni.regione.veneto.it returned 404. The legacy path /web/agricoltura-e-foreste/bollettini-viticoli is a real HTTP 302 to the fitosanitario path, same 258197 bytes, not an older copy. I did NOT establish that pre-2024 bulletins never existed — only that the live site does not expose them.

VOLUME PROVEN AND LISTED (not downloaded): 2025 year page carries 125 dated bulletin links (vine 20, fruit 29, vegetable 42, olive 33, sugar beet 1); 2026 carries 98 (vine 20, fruit 25, vegetable 22, olive 31). The 40 vine URLs are written to MANIFEST-F1a-vine.json.

blockers.detail: Not an access blocker - the file downloads fine at HTTP 200. It is a PARSING trap. All four vine PDFs I downloaded carry /Encrypt with /Filter/Standard (standard security handler, permission restrictions). A naive zlib/regex stream reader inflates 0 or 1 of ~44 streams and returns 0 characters of text, which looks exactly like a scanned image-only PDF. I made that mistake mid-run and corrected it. pdftotext (poppler, present here at /mingw64/bin/pdftotext) opens all four without a password and yields 6373-8561 characters each. Any collector that extracts with a raw parser will record these bulletins as empty and silently report a false zero.

The whole 2025 season lives on a second host, sharing.regione.veneto.it, a Nextcloud instance. No login and no CAPTCHA - I fetched both the landing page (27609 bytes HTML) and the file (append /download, resolves to public.php/dav/files/{token}/, 1984877 bytes application/pdf). The risk is that share tokens are opaque and revocable: they cannot be reconstructed and are not derivable from the date or issue number, so if the index page changes the 2025 corpus becomes unreachable. The 20 tokens must be preserved from the index page, which I have done in MANIFEST-F1a-vine.json.

This per-crop page holds only 2024 (21 date tokens, all 2024; 0 for 2023). A web-search snippet asserted the same page carries 28.04.2023, 19.04.2023, 12.04.2023 and 05.04.2023. I treated that snippet as data and tested it: the live page has no 2023 dates. The most consistent reading is that the per-crop pages are rewritten each season, so earlier years were destroyed in place rather than archived. I did not verify this against any archive service, so it is a hypothesis, not a measurement.

The official site search cannot reach the bulletins. Measured, not inferred: the vine page contains 'Oidio' 44 times and 'Peronospora' 40 times, but a search for 'oidio' returns 3 results and 'peronospora' returns 7, and that page is in neither result set. Anyone who concludes from this search that Veneto publishes no vine disease bulletins would be recording a false zero. Secondary traps in the same endpoint: multi-word queries are a loose OR sorted by date (2430-3314 results of pure noise), and Italian 'vite' also means 'lives', so 'vite peronospora' surfaces a firefighters' book titled 'Salvare Vite'.

not_known: Whether Regione del Veneto published vine bulletins BEFORE 2024. I proved only that the live site does not expose them: bollettini-fitosanitari-2019 through -2023 all return HTTP 404, and a 2027 control returns the same 404, so the probe tests the URL pattern rather than the existence of the documents. Absence of evidence is not evidence of absence.

The paging parameter names of the site search. The results page renders a numbered pager (Primo / Precedente / 1..5 / Successivo / Ultimo) but I never fetched page 2, so I cannot say how to walk past the first 15 results.

Page counts of the four downloaded PDFs. The /Type /Page objects sit inside encrypted object streams, my raw counter returned 0 for two files and 4 for another, and I did not run a page-aware tool. NOT_KNOWN.

Whether the bulletin PDFs have a usable text layer on every page or only on some. pdftotext returned 6373-8561 characters per file, which proves a text layer exists, but each PDF also embeds 22-52 images (charts, phenology photos, trap graphs) whose content is not in that text. I did not check for pages that are image-only.
Whether the 2025 Nextcloud share tokens are permanent or expiring. I fetched two of them successfully today; I have no evidence about their lifetime.
Whether the earlier-year content survives anywhere off-portal (Wayback Machine, Veneto Agricoltura, ARPAV). I stayed inside regione.veneto.it as assigned and did not probe any archive service.
The real filenames the server assigns to the Nextcloud downloads. I saved them under names I chose; I did not capture the Content-Disposition header.

Contents of the remaining 36 vine bulletins (20 for 2026 and 20 for 2025 minus the 4 sampled). Their URLs are proven to be LISTED on index pages I fetched, but the URLs themselves were never fetched, so they are not proven to resolve.
Whether the 'colture erbacee' series, which the 2025 page hands off to Veneto Agricoltura, contains vine content. I did not follow that link.
The bollettini-orticoli-industriali and bollettini-olivicoli per-crop pages for 2024 - I fetched viticoli, frutticoli and seminativi but not those two.

Difesa integrata Sergio Carraro, tel 0444 337085. Note this needs the user's approval before any message is sent - I did not contact anyone.

Do not build any collector on top of the site search at /web/guest/ricerca for this material. It does not index /web/fitosanitario/ and will return a confident, wrong zero. Walk the navigation tree from https://www.regione.veneto.it/web/fitosanitario/bollettini-fitosanitari instead, and re-check each April whether a new year page has appeared and whether the oldest one has been dropped.

Harvest the sibling crop series from the same two year pages while the tokens are live: 2025 carries 125 dated bulletins (fruit 29, vegetable 42, olive 33, sugar beet 1 alongside the 20 vine) and 2026 carries 98 (fruit 25, vegetable 22, olive 31). Same fetch mechanics, no extra discovery needed.

Also capture the adjacent Disciplinari di Produzione Integrata series at /web/fitosanitario/difesa-integrata plus /disciplinari-2025 and /disciplinari-2024 (all fetched HTTP 200; 2023 is 404). These are the regional treatment standards the bulletins refer to, and they show the same disappearing three-year window.

When parsing crop or disease from these documents, key on the Italian common names actually used - Peronospora, Oidio, Botrite, Tignoletta, Flavescenza dorata, Escoriosi, Marciume acido - and not on Latin binomials. I measured 0 occurrences of both 'Erysiphe' and 'Plasmopara' in the bulletin corpus, and the site search for 'Erysiphe necator' returns 'Nessun risultato'.

Keep the collector on the Italian VPN. I confirmed local egress as Milan / country IT / AS208172 Proton AG before every fetch in this run, and I did not test whether any of these hosts behave differently from outside Italy.
